list_windows.description: All open windows with their class, title and workspace.

list_workspaces.description: All workspaces, their monitor and window counts.

focus_window.description: Focus a window by its class or title.

launch_app.description: Launch an installed application; also 'terminal', 'browser', 'files', or the agent TUIs 'hermes'/'codex'/'opencode'.

launch_agent.description: Open a visible agent TUI (hermes/codex/opencode) with the spoken prompt submitted, so the user can watch it work.

set_volume.description: Set speaker volume to a percent (0-100).

get_system_status.description: OS, kernel, hostname, uptime, memory, time.

read_window.description: OCR a window and return its text - used to read back what an app/agent produced.

find_element.description: Locate a UI element by name using the window's accessibility tree (role, label, position). Read-only; prefer over OCR when a control has a clear label.

find_text.description: Find text on screen by OCR and return its screen x,y so you can click it. The coordinate half of read_screen: use it when a control has no accessibility label (a video thumbnail, a canvas, anything inside Chrome). Then pointer_move to x,y and mouse_click. Read-only.

describe_actions.description: Answer 'what can I do here?' for a window: read its accessibility tree and name the 3-5 meaningful actions (open, save, send, delete, navigate), best first. Read-only, no click. Use when the user asks what they can do in the current window, or what is on screen, or to orient before clicking.

describe_outcome.description: Answer "did it work?" about a GUI action: read the window and judge whether the goal is now satisfied; returns a `spoken` sentence to read aloud. Read-only, never clicks.

browser_read.description: Read the current browser page as real DOM elements (role, name, clickable) instead of OCR. Exact where read_screen guesses. Read-only, no mouse movement. Use whenever the browser is the window in question; optional goal narrows it (e.g. 'the search box').

browser_click.description: Click a link/button on the current browser page by name, through the browser's own DOM. No OCR and no pointer movement - it runs in the background, so no takeover announcement is needed. Use this instead of click_element for anything inside Chrome. Verifies URL/title and reports verified honestly.

browser_open_visible_video.description: Play a named video already visible on the current YouTube page. Matches the live video title, Jev confirms the selection, clicks and verifies the exact watch URL. Never searches the web or opens another title; reports visible titles if absent.

youtube_player_state.description: Read the open YouTube watch player's play/pause, time, volume, speed, fullscreen, captions, theater and autoplay state. Read-only.

youtube_player_control.description: Control the open YouTube player: play, pause, skip backward/forward, seek, restart, player volume/mute, speed, fullscreen, captions, theater, autoplay or next video. Verifies player state; background, no mouse movement.

browser_type.description: Type text into a field on the current browser page, found by name (or the only text field). No pointer movement. Use for search boxes and ordinary forms; NEVER for password, payment or authentication fields.

browser_navigate.description: Navigate the browser's current tab to an http(s) URL. Prefer open_url for opening a new page; use this to change the page the agent is already working in.

browser_search.description: General web lookup only: navigate to search results and verify they loaded. Never use to play a video already visible on YouTube; use browser_open_visible_video.

click_element.description: Find a UI element by name and click it via the accessibility tree. Moves the real mouse and takes focus for a moment - announce this to the user first. double=true opens an item.

do_gui_task.description: Run a short, bounded, verified GUI task in one window when simple primitives are not enough (e.g. 'open the Downloads folder', 'fill the name field and submit'). Each step is chosen from options built from the window's live state, acted on, then re-read to confirm what changed. Literal text must be passed in `inputs`; never invented. Returns status done/blocked/needs_agent and never a false success. Use for a handful of steps, not a long march.

do_sequence.description: Run several GUI steps in order in one request, stopping at the first step that cannot be verified and naming it. Returns per-step results and a `spoken` summary.

macro_record.description: Record a desktop chore once so it can be replayed by name. action=start/stop/list/delete.

macro_replay.description: Replay a saved macro by name: re-runs its recorded steps, re-targets live elements, verifies each step, and stops honestly at the failing step. Returns a `spoken` summary.

pointer_move.description: Move the mouse pointer (absolute x,y, or a delta with relative=true).

mouse_click.description: Click the left/right/middle button at the pointer (optionally double).

mouse_scroll.description: Scroll a window (or the pointer's location) up/down/left/right by pages.

move_active_window_to_workspace.description: Move the focused window to a numbered workspace.

close_active_window.description: Close the focused application window (asks you to confirm first).

open_url.description: Open an http(s) URL in the default browser.

type_text.description: Focus a window and type text (optionally press Enter to send). Used to hand prompts to the user's coding agent window ('opencode').

confirm_pending.description: Run the action that is waiting for confirmation.

cancel_pending.description: Discard the action that is waiting for confirmation.

watch_start.description: Watch a window and report when a condition becomes true. Read-only. Returns a job_id to poll with watch_check.

watch_check.description: Check a watch job: status running/met/timeout/stopped plus a `spoken` sentence when done.

market_status.description: Current MarketOS market snapshot: NQ, ES, yields, dollar, VIX and the next major event. Use for 'what's happening with NQ?', 'how's the market?'. Read-only, never triggers analysis.

market_brief.description: A prepared concise MarketOS briefing from existing state and the latest stored analysis. Use for 'give me the market brief', 'catch me up'. Never starts a new analysis.

market_next_event.description: The next important economic event (CPI, NFP, FOMC) with New York time and, when available, consensus and previous. Use for 'what's next?', 'when is CPI?'. Never invents consensus.

market_calendar.description: Economic calendar events, prioritising critical and high importance. Use for 'what's on the calendar today?', 'what's important this week?'.

market_macro.description: Latest macro readings (CPI, employment, growth, policy). Use for 'what's the macro picture?', 'what was the latest CPI?'. Optional series filter e.g. 'CPI'.

market_technical.description: Deterministic NQ technical state: price, VWAP position, overnight and previous levels, structure, opening range, ATR, NQ-versus-ES. Use for 'what's the technical picture?', 'where are we versus VWAP?'. Read-only.

market_latest_events.description: Important market and geopolitical events MarketOS has ranked as material. Use for 'any important news?', 'what just happened?'. Not a raw feed.

market_latest_analysis.description: The latest stored MarketOS analyst result, preferring synthesis. Use for 'what's the latest analysis?', 'what does MarketOS think?'.

market_event_analysis.description: MarketOS analyses stored for one event. Pass an event_id when known, otherwise a short descriptor of the recent event and MarketOS resolves it. Use for 'explain that CPI release'. Never invents an event.

market_usage.description: MarketOS reasoning usage and estimated cost (decisions plus analysis) for the trailing window. Use for 'what is MarketOS costing me today?'. Separate from voice billing.

open_marketos.description: Open or focus the MarketOS workstation at a page: overview, macro, calendar, technical, news, analysts. Use for 'open MarketOS', 'open technicals', 'show me today's calendar'. Focuses an existing window rather than duplicating it.

market_latest_briefing.description: A prepared MarketOS briefing already produced by the workflow layer (pre-market, event preview, post-release recap, FOMC reaction, context change, session recap). Use for 'give me the morning brief', 'give me the latest briefing', 'what happened after the Fed?', 'give me the session recap'. Retrieves an existing briefing; never starts new analysis.

market_history_query.description: A descriptive historical statistic from MarketOS's own stored outcomes: how NQ behaved after comparable past events. Use for 'how has NQ behaved after hot CPI releases?', 'when yields jump after CPI what usually happens?'. Returns a sample size and median moves; never a trading recommendation, never a prediction.

market_materiality_calibration.description: How MarketOS's own materiality levels have behaved historically: sample size and median absolute move per level. Use for 'how have HIGH materiality events behaved?'. Descriptive only.

market_fomc_history.description: Historical FOMC behaviour: how the initial statement move behaved afterwards, with sample size. Use for 'how often does the initial FOMC move reverse?'. Statement and press-conference stages are measured separately.

market_similar_cases.description: Deterministic historical-similarity search: which past MarketOS anchors most resemble the current market context, with each match's later NQ outcome. Use for 'find situations similar to the current market', 'have we seen this kind of CPI setup before?', 'what happened in similar cases?'. The match is computed by code, never guessed; outcomes are context, not a prediction.

market_calibration_review.description: Whether MarketOS recommends reviewing any of its own thresholds, from deterministic calibration statistics. Use for 'does MarketOS recommend reviewing anything?', 'show calibration issues', 'is any threshold miscalibrated?'. Recommendations are for a human and no change is ever applied automatically.
